merged.title: feat: export interface textures and held weapons from the launcher
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
## Before
Texture pack makers had to play the game with dumping on to get the HUD, menu, font and effect textures. Weapon and gadget models had to be found level by level.

## After
- **Models and textures → Interface textures**: the launcher plays the game's routes hidden for a few minutes (**Make**, by kind: Font, HUD and menus, Effects) and writes a run file. **Export** then rebuilds every texture from the player's own disc in under a second, named the way texture packs name them.
- **Weapons and gadgets** in the model export: every item Ratchet holds or wears, each from the first level that has it (rac1 and rac2).
- The project ships no run file. Each player makes their own.

## How
- The port notes how each interface texture is made, plus the disc sectors the game reads (`--interface-run`). At exit it finds each source blob on the disc, also inside WAD streams. A run file holds only hashes, registers and disc offsets, with no game bytes.
- `--interface-export` reads the blobs back

merged.title: fix(renderer): resolve PCSX2 texture pack stutter
merged.author: WeeDoogie
merged.untrustedBody:
While playing I was having hitches with a PCSX2 texture pack used. Was fine when the PCSX2 texture pack was turned off. These changes resolve the hitching I was having and gameplay is smooth.

Work is similar work to https://github.com/OpenRAC/OpenRAC/commit/d1628f479a2377c18c20fc705a8cd224d4017613 but on the PCSX2 side.

**Before**: In a scripted Novalis run with a PCSX2 pack, 713 distinct textures were read 2,784 times. 642 ms of decoding was in the session and the worst single load was 5.3 ms.

**After**: 713 decodes and 2,071 cache hits. Decodes in the session changed from 642 ms to 390 ms and no file was decoded twice.

merged.title: feat(sdk): a hook point called as the game calls it, interface 1.21
merged.author: farfeduc
merged.untrustedBody:
A mod that does what the game does at a hook point sometimes wants the other mods' hooks there to apply. A mod's own weapon takes its rounds as the game's weapons do, and another mod's infinite ammo should cover it too. Until now the only way was `function()` with the game function's name in one disc's build (`FUN_L00_00233db8` on NTSC-U for `rac1.weapon.take_ammo`). That is another name on each disc, and nothing says that the function it returns goes through the hook chain.

Interface 1.21 adds one call at the end of the table:

- `hook_entry(name, signature)` finds the hook point as `hook` does (its id, name or an alias) and checks the signature the same way (`i32` and `u32` are one). It returns the function the game calls there: hooks.c's entry, by the point's symbol, which runs the mods' replacements (the mod loaded last first) and then the game's own function.

  - It returns null for a hook point this OpenRAC lacks, another signature, or no functi

merged.title: fix(frontend): hold frames to the game's tick while the window is in the background
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
On Windows, a RAC1/RAC2 window that isn't focused tanks the whole computer's frame rate. The compositor stops pacing a window that isn't in front, so the swap returns at once and the frames run unbounded.

While the window has no focus, each frame now sleeps (a real sleep, not a spin) until a game tick after the last one. The game keeps its speed in the background and stops taking the GPU and CPU from everything else. Focused play is unchanged.

Not tested on Windows yet.

merged.title: perf: drop the world's depth and the frame's MSAA samples once resolved
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before**
With AA on Vulkan, the multisampled frame was stored to memory every frame and then read again by a separate resolve. The world copy before the HUD also stored the frame's depth. At 3120x1440 with 4x AA that is about 144 MB of extra memory traffic a frame on a phone's tiled GPU (big FPS drops on Batalia with many ships in the air).

**After**
- The pass that last draws the frame resolves it and does not store the samples. That is the world copy when the HUD draws nothing on the frame, or else the end of the frame.
- A tick drawn over the last picture first gets the resolved colour put back into the samples.
- The depth is dropped before the world copy when no HUD draw tests it.

**How**
- `vkgl::resolve_dropping_samples` resolves in the open pass with the colour store dropped.
- `FrameBuffer` tracks dropped samples (`samples_dropped`, `restore_samples`).
- The renderer reports `hud_draws` / `hud_reads_depth` from the HUD's `prepare()`.

**Tested**
- Batalia, AA 4x, 960x540:

merged.title: fix(renderer): black screen under Vulkan on a Mac, and Metal stays Metal with HDR on
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Going Commando drew a black screen on a Mac (sound and logic running), with Metal chosen and HDR on.

- **HDR overrode the renderer.** HDR is Vulkan-only, so with HDR on the game switched to Vulkan ("HDR output is on: drawing with Vulkan") even though Metal was chosen. A chosen Metal now stays Metal and draws in SDR, saying so once in the log.
- **Vulkan on a Mac drew nothing.** MoltenVK translates the shaders to Metal's shading language, where a `float` converts to a vector implicitly. So `environment_specular_surface_frame` and `environment_specular`, each overloaded on a float or `vec3` `f0`, were ambiguous there. They now have one name per type (`environment_specular_surface_frame_scalar`, `environment_specular_rgb`).

Tests on an M5 Max: `texture_filter_on_vulkan`, `enhanced_rendering_vulkan` and `water_gpu`, which failed on develop before, now pass. `renderer_shader_vulkan`, `renderer_shader_metal`, `metal_shader` and `texture_filter_metal` also pass.

merged.title: feat(renderer): HDR output on the Metal renderer (macOS EDR)
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
HDR output on the Metal renderer, so Metal and Vulkan both offer HDR on a Mac.

## How it works

- **Layer.** When HDR is on and the window's display has EDR headroom (SDL's reading of NSScreen's `maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue`, or the potential one, above 1), the window's `CAMetalLayer` gets `wantsExtendedDynamicRangeContent = YES`, `MTLPixelFormatRGBA16Float`, `kCGColorSpaceExtendedLinearSRGB` and `framebufferOnly = NO`. SDR gives it back BGRA8 and its own colour space. The layer changes at once, so HDR turns on and off while the game runs (no restart on Metal), and the frontend asks again when the window moves to another display or the display's HDR state changes (the existing `SDL_EVENT_WINDOW_DISPLAY_CHANGED` / `HDR_STATE_CHANGED` handling).
- **Encode.** `present()` runs the Vulkan backend's own encode pass, `renderer/vulkan/shaders/hdr_encode.comp` in its scRGB form, straight into the drawable instead of the SDR flip. It is compiled by the Vulkan backend's glsla

merged.author: Veradictus

Going Commando compares `experience >> 5` with its upgrade steps (and nanotech XP with its health table the same way), so the editor showed counts 32 times bigger than the goals. A RYNO II set to 23,000 was really 718.

- Weapon and nanotech XP are shown and taken in the compared units: read `raw >> 5`, write `shown << 5`. A value left alone is not written, so its low 5 bits stay and an untouched save keeps its bytes.

opened.author: Veradictus
opened.untrustedBody:
HDR output on the Metal renderer, so Metal and Vulkan both offer HDR on a Mac.

## How it works

- **Layer.** When HDR is on and the window's display has EDR headroom (SDL's reading of NSScreen's `maximumExtendedDynamicRangeColorComponentValue`, or the potential one, above 1), the window's `CAMetalLayer` gets `wantsExtendedDynamicRangeContent = YES`, `MTLPixelFormatRGBA16Float`, `kCGColorSpaceExtendedLinearSRGB` and `framebufferOnly = NO`. opened.author: Clank700
opened.untrustedBody:
Fixes the crash `read at game address 0x50000010` (`func_001F9A98 <- space.c:2425`) that shows up after **Load** from the start menu and when travelling by ship, roughly one try in three or four. `initialize_level_runtime` in `space.c` reaches two globals by adding a byte offset to unrelated ones:

On every later transition a level overlay is loaded and these globals relocate by different amounts, so the two writes hit unrelated level data and `current_vu_chain` keeps the previous level's value (`0x60000` on Kalebo III, not `0x100000`)

opened.author: farfeduc
opened.untrustedBody:
`relocate()` turns an executable global into its address in the loaded level, using the pairs its functions' code gives. An address that no pair is near (within 0x100 below it) and no code forms was kept as it was.

RAC1's pause screens (0x001CEA80 on NTSC-U) are such an address: the game reaches them through a pointer. In a level they stayed at the executable's address, where other data lies, so a mod writing there through `relocate()` corrupted the level's data.

When the nearest pairs below and above such an address moved by the same amount, the data between them moved as one block, and the address now moves with them. In level 1, 0x1CE798 and 0x1CEC20 both moved by -0x1BA80, so the pause screens are at 0x1B3000.

Between pairs that moved apart, nothing says where the data went, and the address is kept as before. `OPENRAC_TRACE_RELOCATION` names the pairs around each such address.

## Summary

Add `tools/audit_pal_relocs.py` to check relocation targets of exact `src/pal/` functions after the PAL map is updated.
